title: Which queue is better?
hook: One order waits less, the other is late less. Which one is better?

knows: reading short labels and comparing simple counts
doesNotKnow: that task orders trade off measures such as total waiting and missed deadlines, so the measure that matters has to be chosen before one order can be called better

misconception: One order of tasks can be best on every measure at once.
objective: Compare waiting and deadline misses for one fixed order.

claims.text: Scenario, hook and prediction: One order waits less, the other is late less. Which one is better? What is required before calling an order better? Options: Count visible movement / Choose the objective. Correct option: Choose the objective. All fixture labels, example words, dates, task durations and file fields are stipulated exercise data.
